walkthroughs.body_html:
Inorganic Chemistry — a core area of A-Level Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Inorganic Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Inorganic Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which of these Group 2 metals reacts most vigorously with water?
options: Barium
Magnesium
Calcium
Beryllium

mcqs.q: Adding acidified silver nitrate to a bromide solution gives:
options: A cream precipitate
A white precipitate
A yellow precipitate
No precipitate

mcqs.q: Which halogen is a liquid at room temperature?
options: Bromine
Chlorine
Iodine
Fluorine

mcqs.q: Going down Group 7, the oxidising power of the halogens:
options: Decreases
Increases
Stays the same
First increases then decreases

mcqs.q: Why does atomic radius decrease across a period?
options: Radius decreases because the number of shells decreases across a period.
Nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same shell with similar shielding, so the electrons are pulled in closer.
Radius decreases because atoms have fewer electrons across a period.
Halogens can never displace each other from solution.

mcqs.q: Which halogens can displace which halides from solution?
options: Halogens can never displace each other from solution.
Iodine displaces chloride because larger halogens are more reactive, like Group 1 metals.
Radius decreases because the number of shells decreases across a period.
A halogen displaces the halide of any element below it in the group — chlorine displaces bromide and iodide ions.

mcqs.q: What gas is given off when Group 2 metals react with water?
options: Group 2 metals give off carbon dioxide with water.
Group 2 metals react with water to release oxygen gas.
Halogens can never displace each other from solution.
Hydrogen — the metal forms a hydroxide and hydrogen gas, e.g. Ca + 2H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ + H₂.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Halogen displacement”?
options: Group 2 metals react with water with increasing vigour down the group, forming hydroxides and hydrogen gas.
A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halide from solution; chlorine displaces both bromide and iodide ions.
Atomic radius decreases across a period as nuclear charge increases with no extra shielding, and increases down a group.
The halogens become less volatile down the group as van der Waals' forces strengthen: chlorine is a gas, bromine a liquid, iodine a solid.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Halogen volatility”?
options: A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halide from solution; chlorine displaces both bromide and iodide ions.
Acidified silver nitrate gives a white precipitate with chloride ions, cream with bromide and yellow with iodide.
The halogens become less volatile down the group as van der Waals' forces strengthen: chlorine is a gas, bromine a liquid, iodine a solid.
Calcium gives a brick-red flame, strontium a crimson flame and barium a green flame, identifying their compounds.
